subject: Emergency Image Revocation & Signing Rotation for Air-Isolated Deploys
messages:
From: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emergency Image Revocation & Signing Rotation for Air-Isolated Deploys

Jasmine / Marcus —

We discovered an incorrect launcher config (v2.14) that was pushed to an islanded customer site last night (no outbound connectivity). The site admin has isolated the appliance but cannot pull a replacement image. Customer (ACME Manufacturing) is asking for two things: an immediate way to revoke the bad image so local ops will stop autostarting it, and a documented emergency pullback + re-image procedure that works when the site is completely air-isolated.

Key constraints:
- No direct internet from the appliance (air-isolated)
- Only USB media or couriered signed bundle can be used for updates
- Customer wants cryptographic proof the image is revoked and that any successor image is signed by Redwood keys

Can you confirm whether we have an established signed-revocation manifest format and whether we support a short-lived revocation token that on-site staff can apply? If not, can we draft a plan and a one-page checklist for ops to follow? ACME is asking for ETA on the remediation docs and any emergency key-rotation steps.

Contact at ACME: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.example> (cc'd internally)

Thanks,
ACME CloudOps

Attachment: none

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency Image Revocation & Signing Rotation for Air-Isolated Deploys

Hi Raj / ACME team —

Sorry to hear about the bad launcher config. We have an internal lightweight revocation process for air-isolated sites but it's not documented end-to-end for customers, and we should treat this as high priority. Proposed immediate plan:

1) Produce a signed revocation manifest (signed-manifest-example.json) that the site can apply locally. The manifest will contain: image-id, revoked=true, revocation-reason, timestamp, signature, key-id.
2) Ship a replacement signed image bundle (via courier) with an operator checklist to perform re-image and verification.
3) If necessary, perform an emergency signing-key rotation: generate a short-lived rotation key and include rotation metadata in the bundle.

Requests for Redwood team:
- Karthik: can you confirm the manifest schema and commands the appliance will run to validate a revocation manifest? Also advise on HSM/KMS restrictions for generating short-lived rotation signatures.
- Marissa: can you draft a one-page ops checklist + an internal playbook we can attach to the courier package?
- Marcus: can you confirm we have a forensic artifact collection step for the on-site admin to capture logs before the re-image?

ACME: ETA from our side is 24–48 hours for the initial revocation manifest and checklist. We'll coordinate courier timelines once you confirm the physical handoff.

I'll consolidate and send a formal playbook for sign-off.

— Jasmine Liu
Lead, Private Deployments (Redwood Inference)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency Image Revocation & Signing Rotation for Air-Isolated Deploys

Jasmine / team / Raj —

Attached is a first-draft playbook (revocation-playbook-v1.pdf) and a short pullback checklist (pullback-checklist.xlsx). Highlights and responsibilities:

- Step 0: Customer isolates appliance and confirms serial + checksum of the currently running image. (Ops)
- Step 1: Redwood produces a signed revocation manifest (signed-manifest-example.json) and provides it to ACME via secure courier. (Redwood: Karthik / Security)
- Step 2: On-site applies revocation manifest to local image store; appliance checks signature against embedded root key (appliance has root public key pinned). If revoked=true, appliance will not autostart the image. (On-site Ops)
- Step 3: On-site follow pullback checklist to stop services, dump KV cache, and collect logs. (On-site Ops + Redwood remote guidance if connectivity exists)
- Step 4: Physical install of replacement signed bundle; run verification steps (hash check, signature verification). (On-site Ops)
- Step 5: Post-mortem and evidence handoff to Redwood for root-cause and potential CI/CD rollback. (Redwood + ACME)

Emergency signing-key rotation guidance (short form):
- We should avoid rotating root keys unless absolutely necessary. Instead, issue a short-lived rotation cert signed by the current root. Rotation cert metadata includes: rotation-id, valid-from, valid-until, new-key-fingerprint, signing-policy. Rotation cert and signed-manifest are included in the couriered bundle.
- If root compromise is suspected, escalate to Security with full HSM-backed rekey process and contact legal.

Open items:
- Karthik: need precise CLI snippets for manifest signing & verification that run on the security appliance (we will include as a one-liner in the playbook).
- Marcus: confirm what logs we need in the forensic bundle and whether we should include a pre-built log-collector USB image.

ACME: can you confirm courier window and whether they have an on-site engineer who can follow the attached checklist?

Attachments: revocation-playbook-v1.pdf, pullback-checklist.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Operations (Redwood Inference)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency Image Revocation & Signing Rotation for Air-Isolated Deploys

Marissa / Jasmine / Raj —

Confirmed, we have a minimal revocation manifest schema and a signing CLI. I'll paste the relevant snippets here and will also push the one-liner to the playbook draft in Drive.

Manifest (JSON, short example):
{
  "image_id": "redwood-appliance:v2.14",
  "revoked": true,
  "reason": "launcher-config-bug-20260406",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-07T16:50:00Z",
  "key_id": "rwd-root-2022",
  "signature": "<base64sig>"
}

Signing (server-side HSM) — example: 
# sign-manifest.sh (uses HSM key rwd-root-2022)
cat manifest.json | rwd-sign --key-id rwd-root-2022 --hsm-slot 1 > signed-manifest.json

Verification (on-appliance one-liner):
curl --silent --unix-socket /var/run/rwd-verify.sock -X POST -d @signed-manifest.json \n  http://localhost:8080/verify-manifest | jq -r '.valid'

Rotation guidance:
- Short-lived rotation certs are created by the HSM and signed by the root; they have a maximum TTL of 72 hours for emergency bundles. Include rotation metadata in signed-manifest.json under "rotation":{...}.
- On the appliance, verification checks both signature chain and TTL for rotation certs; expired rotation certs are rejected.

Forensic artifacts: include /var/log/redwood/*, /etc/rwd/config.yaml, kernel dmesg output, and a copy of the running image hash. If we want a more turn-key approach, Marcus can prepare a USB image with a log-collector.

I'll sync the CLI examples into the Drive link Jasmine created and finalize the signed-manifest template. ETA: I'll push the updated signed-manifest-example.json and CLI snippets within 6 hours.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
